newsitem.title: UK: Euro LIBOR will smooth transition for derivatives.
newsitem.headline: Euro LIBOR will smooth transition for derivatives.

text.p: A recent proposal to replicate euro LIBOR for displaced national currencies will greatly smooth the derivatives industry's transition to the European Union's planned single currency, a leading market figure said on Wednesday.
Daily production of separate London interbank offered rates (LIBOR) for displaced currencies would be a largely academic exercise after EMU, said the source who preferred to remain anonymous.

"But there will be corporates out there who will want a mark LIBOR or a franc LIBOR rate quoted until 2002. The easiest thing is to just copy the euro rate and publish that which is what has been proposed," he said.
"This continuity of contract is the key thing."

The British Bankers' Association (BBA) said on June 4 it was proposing a euro LIBOR interest reference rate as a benchmark from January 1, 1999 and that participating national currency LIBOR rates should be the same as those for euro LIBOR.

This seeming resolution of continuity of contract for LIBOR-based instruments still left many others which specify reference rates such as FIBOR and PIBOR (Frankfurt and Paris IBOR respectively) which are sponsored by other entities, the derivatives source said.
Earlier today, the International Swaps and Derivatives Association published a report calling on providers of price sources to announce their strategy for the euro by July 31.
"There is an urgent need for price sponsors to announce their plans for the euro transition," ISDA chairman Gay Evans said in a statement.
Evans said markets needed to be able to "effectively start to examine the business, systems and legal implications of the changeover from national currency to euro rates".
The ISDA report called on the European Monetary Institute to monitor the disappearance of price sources, especially where they were sponsored by central banks.

"There is a strong possibility that a number of national price sources will be disbanded and that a single panel for all (or possibly just part) of the EMU area will come into existence to provide euro quotations," the report said.
"The question remains as to whether, for existing contracts, national currency rates quoted by a national pricing panel could be succeeded by a euro rate quoted by a different panel."
The ISDA report also called on its members to submit their views relating to the changeover of price sources.

The third stage of economic and monetary union, including the introduction of the European Union's planned single currency, the euro, is prescribed by EU law to take place no later than January 1, 1999.
But euro currencies will not be completely phased out until 2002, by when notes and coins will be replaced.
LIBOR is the cost of short-term money as quoted by London-based banks in a host of currencies and compiled by the BBA.
